summary: This bill allows taxpayers to count up to $500 ($1,000 for joint filers) spent on basic water safety and swimming lessons, and related equipment, as a medical expense for tax deduction purposes, excluding competitive training.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow qualified water competency and water safety lesson expenses to be treated as medical expenses, which are tax-deductible. This change would effectively lower the taxable income for individuals who incur these expenses, thus leading to lower tax revenue for the government.
